MnIn₂Se₄ and Mn₂In₂Se₅: calculation vs experiment

Phonon dispersion, intrinsic κ(T), comparison with the hot-pressed measurements, and the 3-phonon and disorder scattering rates at 300 K. All numbers come from files already in this repository (see PROGRESS_REPORT_20261118.md); only the Mn₂In₂Se₅ dispersion is interpolated here from its committed fc2.hdf5.

Why a second table. The pellets are only partly textured, so Perp is not pure in-plane and Para is not pure κ_zz: part of the in-plane conduction leaks into Para (this is why Para / κ_zz ratios above look smaller). The average (2·Perp + Para)/3 equals (2·κ_in-plane + κ_zz)/3 for any texture, so it compares calculation and experiment without knowing the texture.

The single-crystal κ is 3–4× above the hot-pressed samples. Antisite disorder (VCA) closes part of the gap; the rest needs a nanoscale effective mean free path (L_eff ≈ 10–50 nm, §8); the possible reasons are discussed in §9. The L3 model of §8 is not listed here: it is fitted to these experimental points, so at 300 K it reproduces them by construction.

Which material is lower: Mn₂In₂Se₅ relative to MnIn₂Se₄

In the experiment Mn₂In₂Se₅ is lower in both directions. The calculation reproduces this in-plane and in the direction average, but not for κ_zz. ✓ / ✗: same / opposite sign as the experiment.

300 K, Mn₂In₂Se₅ vs MnIn₂Se₄in-plane / Perpκ_zz / Paradirection average
experiment, Perp / Para (303 K)-21 %-34 %-23 %
calculation, value to quote, in-plane / κ_zz-28 % ✓+53 % ✗-22 % ✓
calculation, ordered RTA 20³, in-plane / κ_zz-19 % ✓+54 % ✗-13 % ✓
calculation, value to quote mixed with the texture s → Perp / Para-22 % ✓-23 % ✓-22 % ✓
  • κ_zz should not be compared with Para directly. Para contains part of the in-plane conduction, Para = s·κ_in-plane + (1−s)·κ_zz. With the same s for both materials, Mn₂In₂Se₅ has the lower Para as soon as s > 0.22. The fitted texture is s = 0.35 (MnIn₂Se₄) and 0.23 (Mn₂In₂Se₅); with it the calculated values give the experimental order in both directions (last row: Para 1.62 vs 2.10). XRD of both pellet faces would measure s independently.
  • The Mn₂In₂Se₅ κ_zz is bounded. Its FC3-cutoff steps (−11.9 %, −9.9 %) are followed by a step of at most −3.3 % (§2.2, hold-out test), so its κ_zz stays about 50 % above MnIn₂Se₄'s within what the data can test.
  • Point defects hardly lower κ_zz. Antisite mass disorder from the ordered to the random limit lowers the in-plane κ by 58 % but κ_zz by only 20 % in Mn₂In₂Se₅ (MnIn₂Se₄, x = 0 → 0.44: by 55 % and 21 %; plot_data/disorder_sweep_300K.csv). κ_zz is carried by low-frequency interlayer acoustic modes, which mass disorder barely scatters. A lower κ_zz in the Mn₂In₂Se₅ pellets therefore points to defects along c, such as stacking faults, polytype intergrowths or secondary phases from its decomposition between 400 and 800 °C (§9, items 1 and 4).

2Calculation setup and convergence

How the force constants were obtained, how far κ is converged in the FC3 cutoff and the q-mesh, and which solver each quoted number comes from. Convergence criterion: a parameter counts as converged when its last refinement step changes κ by less than 10 % (✓ in the tables), the accuracy target of this project. Data: plot_data/convergence_fc3_cutoff.csv, convergence_qmesh.csv, solver_terms.csv.

check of FC2interlayer TA velocity 1348 m/s vs 1338 m/s from the DFT elastic constants (+0.75 %)interlayer TA 1387 m/s, C₄₄ 9.5–10.3 GPa
κ codephono3py (3.24.0 and 4.4.0; same population term in both)
  • For MnIn₂Se₄, FC2 and FC3 come from two different supercells of the same crystal. Both use the identical relaxed cell (same lattice vectors and atomic positions) and the identical DFT input; the INCAR files differ only in the MAGMOM count, and the k-point density is the same (2×2×1 on 4×4×2 and 2×2×2 on 4×4×1 sample the same k-spacing). Only the size of the supercell along c differs.
  • Why two supercells. In the 4×4×1 cell (one unit cell, 13.2 Å along c) each atom meets its own periodic image across the van der Waals gap, which made the interlayer FC2 far too soft: interlayer TA 323 m/s instead of 1338 m/s. The 4×4×2 FC2 fixes this (1348 m/s). Repeating the anharmonic dataset in 4×4×2 would cost about two days of DFT and does not raise the usable FC3 cutoff, so FC3 stays on 4×4×1.
  • How they are combined. phono3py takes FC2 and FC3 on different supercells (phonon_supercell_matrix = 4×4×2 for FC2, supercell_matrix = 4×4×1 for FC3). ShengBTE cannot, so all MnIn₂Se₄ κ values are from phono3py.
  • Mn₂In₂Se₅ needed no second cell: its 4×4×1 FC2 already gives the correct interlayer TA velocity.

300 K, RTA, isotropic N³ meshes (MnIn₂Se₄ isotopes on; Mn₂In₂Se₅ isotopes off, which changes κ by −1.2 % in-plane and −0.4 % κ_zz). In-plane κ is converged (steps below 3 % from 14³ on). The total κ_zz keeps falling by 12–15 % per step: that is a numerical artifact, because the single q-point next to Γ on the Γ–Z line carries 15–50 % of κ_zz on these meshes and its weight shrinks as N⁻³. Leaving that point out gives the converged term, which changes by less than 1 % per step from 14³ (MnIn₂Se₄) and 24³ (Mn₂In₂Se₅). Chosen: κ_zz = converged term, plateau over 14³–30³ (MnIn₂Se₄, 0.648 ± 0.003) and 24³–32³ (Mn₂In₂Se₅, 0.977 ± 0.008 with isotopes); in-plane MnIn₂Se₄ from LBTE at 14³ with the +1.3 % mesh correction measured on the RTA series, Mn₂In₂Se₅ from RTA at 32³. The κ(T) curves use 14³ and 16³, and the VCA comparison uses 20³ for both (within 3 % of the converged values).

2.4 Solvers: RTA, iterative (LBTE) and Wigner

  • RTA (relaxation-time approximation) gives each phonon its own lifetime and treats every scattering event as resistive. It is cheap and gives the mode-resolved data used for the curves, the mesh and cutoff scans and the disorder models.
  • LBTE (phono3py's direct solution of the linearised Boltzmann equation, equivalent to the converged iterative solution of ShengBTE) solves the full collision matrix, so momentum-conserving Normal processes do not destroy the heat current. In-plane it is higher than RTA by 24 % for MnIn₂Se₄ (14³: 4.5219 vs 3.6474) and 5.9 % for Mn₂In₂Se₅ (10³: 2.9879 vs 2.8220). For κ_zz, LBTE and RTA agree to 4·10⁻⁵. The quoted in-plane values are therefore LBTE-based; κ_zz uses RTA.
  • Wigner (Simoncelli, Marzari, Mauri, Nat. Phys. 15, 809 (2019)) splits κ into the usual population (particle-like) term and a coherence (wave-like) term between modes whose frequencies lie closer than their linewidths. It matters in low-κ, many-branch crystals like these. The coherence term was computed in the RTA (Wigner-RTA) and is added to the population value. Its size at 300 K: MnIn₂Se₄ in-plane 0.091, κ_zz 0.066; Mn₂In₂Se₅ in-plane 0.147, κ_zz 0.112 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, i.e. +2–5 % in-plane and +10–12 % κ_zz.
  • Version rule for the coherence term. phono3py 4.4.0 with SMM19 gives a coherence term 12–17× too large for MnIn₂Se₄, because unregularised soft modes near Γ make it diverge; 3.24.0 and the 4.x IBDB19 option agree with each other. MnIn₂Se₄ therefore uses the 3.24.0 value. The Mn₂In₂Se₅ 4.4.0 value passes the same soft-mode test (−0.3 % in κ_zz when modes below 0.3 THz are removed) and is used.

6Scattering rates at 300 K

Largest FC3 cutoff, 20³ mesh, τ⁻¹ = 2Γ. Baseline: real masses + natural isotopes. VCA: averaged site masses + mass-variance scattering. Top row MnIn₂Se₄ (i = 0.44), bottom row Mn₂In₂Se₅ (x = 0.19).

Left: the 3-phonon rates of the ordered and VCA crystals agree within a few tens of percent, because VCA changes the masses, not the anharmonicity. Right: VCA mass-variance scattering is 2–3 orders of magnitude stronger than natural-isotope scattering, rises as ω² at low frequency and flattens at high frequency. Effect on κ at 300 K: MnIn₂Se₄ in-plane 3.69 → 1.49 (2.48×), κ_zz 0.638 → 0.445 (1.43×); Mn₂In₂Se₅ in-plane 3.00 → 1.46 (2.05×), κ_zz 0.984 → 0.753 (1.31×) at x = 0.19 (x = 0.13: 1.63 and 0.792). The weaker effect in Mn₂In₂Se₅ comes from its less mixed sites (81 % pure at x = 0.19, against 56/44 on the MnIn₂Se₄ octahedral site).

  • Lattice and Raman: the relaxed structure is within 0.7 % of the single-crystal XRD values, and the two strong Raman peaks match the calculated A1g modes (all Raman-active modes: Eg 26, A1g 75, Eg 95, Eg 168, A1g 176, A1g 260 cm⁻¹). Both support the force constants.
  • Sound velocity: ultrasonic, hot-pressed pellets, two samples (agree within 2 %). The measured v_L is below the calculated v_L in every direction (c axis 3113 m/s is the lowest), so texture cannot explain it; porosity and defect softening of the pellet are the likely reasons. The pellet density is not known yet (theoretical 5.35 g/cm³), so the two cannot be separated. The propagation direction relative to the pressing axis is also not known.
  • Minimum κ (Cahill, Watson & Pohl, PRB 46, 6131 (1992); diffuson model, Agne et al., Energy Environ. Sci. 11, 609 (2018)), high-temperature limits, n = 0.0376 Å⁻³: diffuson 0.20 and Cahill 0.31 from the measured velocities. The measured κ_tot is above both, as a lattice κ must be: Para (0.49 at 303 K) is 1.6× the Cahill value and Perp (0.93) 3.0×. Cross-plane heat transport in the pellets is thus within a factor of two of the amorphous limit, consistent with the strong extrinsic scattering of the L3 fit (L ≈ tens of nm); in-plane it is not. (Until 2026-11-22 the Cahill value was computed without the factor 1/2 of its high-temperature limit, i.e. twice too high, and the measurement appeared to lie between the two limits.)

8What the L3 fit is

L3 is the extrinsic model of analysis/extrinsic/. Yes, it is fitted to the experimental values, so its agreement with experiment is by construction and is not a prediction. At 300 K it gives Perp / Para = 0.92 / 0.49 (MnIn₂Se₄, measured 0.93 / 0.49) and 0.78 / 0.34 (Mn₂In₂Se₅, measured 0.74 / 0.32). Its purpose is not to supply κ (the measurement already does) but to answer how much extra scattering, and of what kind, turns the calculated single crystal into the measured pellet: the fitted parameters (texture s and boundary length L; the antisite fraction x is taken from structure refinements) are the result, and the 55–145 K points, which were not fitted, test it.

Γ_λ = Γ_3ph,λ(T) + Σ g_elem(x)·B_elem,λ + |v_λ| / (4π L) 3-phonon Mn↔In antisite mass disorder grain boundary (Casimir) κ_Para = s·κ_xx + (1−s)·κ_zz κ_Perp = (1−s/2)·κ_xx + (s/2)·κ_zz
  • Inputs that are not fitted: the first-principles 3-phonon rates, phonon velocities and heat capacities (ordered masses), and the mass-disorder basis rates B, computed once per material on a 24³ mesh.
  • Parameters: x, the fraction of Mn on In sites, fixed at the literature value (below); L, an effective boundary mean free path, and s = ⟨sin²θ⟩, the texture (0 = fully textured, 2/3 = random), fitted.
  • Data used: only the 300–623 K points of experiment/kappa_tot_digitized.csv, both directions. The fit minimises the rms of ln(model/experiment) over L, with s optimised at each point. The 55–145 K points are not used; they only test the model.
  • Result (analysis/disorder/README.md §5.1): MnIn₂Se₄ with x = 0.44 (single-crystal XRD, Range et al., Z. Naturforsch. 46b, 1122 (1991)): L = 30.7 nm, s = 0.35, rms 1.2 %. Mn₂In₂Se₅ with x = 0.19(2) (powder Rietveld of the R-3m phase, Williams et al., J. Mater. Chem. C 12, 1753 (2024), ESI Table S7): L = 22.1 nm, s = 0.23, rms 3.4 %. So L ≈ 20–30 nm in both materials. (The 0.704/0.296 occupancy of Chernoukhov et al., Molecules 30, 1904 (2025) belongs to a different, quenched polymorph, P3̄m1, and is not used.)
  • Why x is fixed: with x free as well, the fit determines only s (acceptable 0.33–0.38 and 0.15–0.28). x and L both push κ down and are degenerate: acceptable x spans 0–0.66 and 0.01–0.50, and the free optimum (x = 0.45, L = 30.7 nm, rms 1.2 %; x = 0.13, L = 15.9 nm, rms 3.2 %) is not evidence for any occupancy. XRD (texture), SEM (grain size) and a Rietveld occupancy refinement of our own pellets would break the degeneracy.
  • Not to be combined with VCA: L3 already contains the antisite scattering through x, so the VCA and L3 curves are alternatives, not additive corrections.
  • κ_e is taken as 0. If the electronic part is not negligible, the fitted extrinsic scattering is too strong.

9Why the calculation lies above the experiment

At 300 K the calculated single-crystal κ is 4.3× above the hot-pressed κ_tot for both materials (direction average, values to quote, §1). Antisite disorder (VCA, at the literature occupancies) brings this down to 1.5× (MnIn₂Se₄) and 2.0× (Mn₂In₂Se₅; RTA, 20³). The candidate reasons for the rest are listed below, roughly in order of how much each can explain, with the evidence and the test. These are hypotheses. Only the first two are quantified here.

#mechanismpossible effect on κevidencehow to test
1Planar defects and grain boundaries: a nanoscale effective mean free path largest; closes the remaining gap with L ≈ 20–30 nm (L3, x fixed from the literature, §8) below 150 K the measured κ is flat, with no 1/T rise, i.e. a temperature-independent scattering dominates; the required L is far below typical hot-pressed grain sizes (0.5–5 μm), which points to stacking faults, twins or polytype intergrowths, common in these layered "124"/"225" compounds; Para κ_tot is only 1.6× the Cahill minimum κ (§7) SEM grain size; TEM/HAADF for stacking faults
2Mn/In antisite disorder VCA at the literature x: in-plane 2.5× (MnIn₂Se₄) / 2.1× (Mn₂In₂Se₅), κ_zz 1.4× / 1.3× at 300 K single-crystal refinement i = 0.44 (Range 1991); Rietveld x = 0.19(2) (Williams 2024); broad Raman modes in Mn₂In₂Se₅ attributed to site disorder (Williams 2024) Rietveld occupancy of our own pellets. VCA counts only the mass difference, so it is a lower bound: bond-strength and local-strain disorder are missing (a disordered supercell would include them). LBTE + coherence for VCA is planned (test/figures/kappa_vs_T/jobs_lbte_wigner/)
3Paramagnetic spin disorder (Mn²⁺, S = 5/2) not known; could be tens of per cent the calculation assumes a static ferromagnetic order; the real crystals are paramagnetic at 300 K and order (antiferromagnetic / spin glass) only below ≈ 6–7 K, with strong antiferromagnetic exchange (Weiss θ ≈ −198 K for Mn₂In₂Se₅, Williams 2024). Fluctuating spins make the exchange-dependent force constants random and add spin–phonon scattering magnetic susceptibility of the pellets; force constants for antiferromagnetic or random spin configurations
4Off-stoichiometry, vacancies, secondary phases not known; cation vacancies scatter far more strongly than a mass substitution MnIn₂Se₄ has a 5–6 mol % homogeneity range towards In₂Se₃ (Mammadov 2025), i.e. cation vacancies; Mn₂In₂Se₅ decomposes into MnIn₂Se₄ + MnSe between about 400 and 800 °C and MnSe admixtures are common (Chernoukhov 2025), so hot pressing in that range may leave secondary phases and interfaces XRD of the pressed pellet (phase purity), EDS composition, hot-pressing temperature and time
5Porosity, pellet softening ≈ 10–20 % for 5–10 % porosity measured sound velocity 20–30 % below the calculation in every direction (§7) Archimedes density
6Higher-order anharmonicity, temperature effects typically −10 to −30 % at 300 K in low-κ layered selenides (not computed here) low-lying optical branches (§3) and strong 3-phonon rates; the calculation uses 0 K harmonic phonons and 3-phonon scattering only four-phonon scattering, temperature-dependent force constants (expensive)
7FC3 cutoff MnIn₂Se₄ ≈ −10 %; Mn₂In₂Se₅ next step ≥ −3.3 % §2.2Mn₂In₂Se₅ done (refit to 7.43 Å + hold-out test); MnIn₂Se₄ the same test on its 7.74 Å refits

Ruled out as explanations

  • Texture moves conduction between Perp and Para, but the direction average (2·Perp + Para)/3 does not depend on it and is still 4.3× too low (§1).
  • Electronic κ_e: the experiment is κ_tot. Subtracting κ_e lowers the experimental lattice κ and widens the gap.
  • Lattice constants: the calculated cell is 0.6–0.7 % larger than measured (§7); a larger cell tends to lower, not raise, the calculated κ.
  • LBTE and coherence raise the calculated κ, so they widen the gap. Digitising errors (±0.005–0.01 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹) are negligible.

Mechanisms 1 and 2 alone already reproduce the data (that is the L3 fit). Every further mechanism (3–6) that is real would reduce the boundary scattering needed. The fitted L ≈ 20–30 nm lumps together all scattering the model leaves out, so the actual spacing of planar defects is at least that large. The cheapest decisive measurements are the pellet density, SEM/TEM of the microstructure and XRD of the pressed pellet.

10Caveats

  • The experimental points are digitised from a figure (±0.005 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at high T, ±0.01 at low T) and are κ_tot with κ_e not subtracted. Replace experiment/kappa_tot_digitized.csv once the raw data are available.
  • Mn₂In₂Se₅: the FC3 cutoff is tested only up to 6.90 Å (next step ≥ −2.1 % / −3.3 %); the existing frames cannot support larger cutoffs. Within that, both orderings hold: in-plane MnIn₂Se₄ 37 % higher, κ_zz Mn₂In₂Se₅ about 50 % higher.
  • Between the 145 K and 300 K experimental points the Para values drop much more than Perp (Mn₂In₂Se₅ −32 % vs −6 %), possibly two instruments or two samples; this is why the fit uses the high-temperature range only.
